text:
tessa: quick feedback session  mobile console touch behaviour + table overflow. i've got a prototype where the sidebar can be swiped open from the left edge on phones. figma: https://figma.com/file/wxyz7890 | curious about edge-swipe conflicts with browser back gesture on iOS. :thinking:

ryan: nice. we should avoid hijacking the system back gesture. on iOS Safari the back swipe area is ~20px from the left edge. maybe require a 24px swipe zone or long-press handle to open instead of full-edge swipe.

nisha: prefer a visible grab-handle at 12px from edge so users discover it. if we keep edge-swipe, add a 2-step threshold: 1) 8px horizontal move, 2) velocity check, otherwise let back gesture win.

mike: adding to that, consider a small affordance dot that is accessible (aria-label="open navigation"). also account for safe-area-inset (notch) on iPhones. css hint: `padding-left: env(safe-area-inset-left);`

ryan: thanks. another thing: tables with many columns  current prototype creates horizontal overflow that hides the row actions. can we implement column prioritization so important columns stay visible and less-important ones collapse into a kebab menu on narrow widths?

tessa: yes, we sketched a priority list: name > status > last run > runtime > tags. lower-priority columns move to expandable details. this avoids tiny columns.

nisha: accessibility: when columns collapse into details, ensure that the row's "details" button has aria-expanded and focuses the panel. keyboard users need a way to open/close without a mouse. also announce changes via live region when layout changes to mobile variant.

mike: perf note: collapsing into a details panel reduces DOM churn for virtualization. we can render a placeholder cell for collapsed columns and lazy-load the details panel.

ryan: for copy/UX text: current mobile tooltip reads "Show more" which is ambiguous. suggestion: use "Show details" and for the grab handle use "Open navigation". short, action-oriented.

nisha: agree. for screen readers add context: "Show details for job <name>".

ryan: quick pseudo for gesture detection i can try in the branch:
```
let startX = 0;
container.addEventListener('touchstart', e => startX = e.touches[0].clientX);
container.addEventListener('touchmove', e => {
  const dx = e.touches[0].clientX - startX;
  if (startX < 24 && dx > 30 && Math.abs(dx) > Math.abs(e.touches[0].clientY - startY)) {
    openSidebar()
  }
})
```

mike: remember to throttle and cancel on horizontal scroll inside tables. also respect pointer-events for nested carousels.

tessa: action items:
- ryan: prototype edge-swipe with safe-area and thresholds, open PR
- nisha: write a11y acceptance criteria (aria labels, live region text, keyboard flow)
- mike: implement column priority behavior and lazy details
- design (me): update comps with grab-handle + condensed row layout
I'll add tasks to the sprint board and link the figma. thanks :heart:

a11y-bot: checklist reminder: ensure focus order, aria-expanded, skip link to main content, 44px minimum touch targets.

nisha: i'll run the mobile screenreader pass once ryan's branch lands. ryan: tag me in the PR.

ryan: will do, testing on Safari iOS and Chrome Android.
